title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 357 (Commencement of winding up by Tribunal)

content.overview: The winding up of a company by the Tribunal shall be deemed to commence at the time of the presentation of the petition for the winding up.
content.glance: Tribunal winding up is deemed to commence at the time of presentation of the winding-up petition.
content.study: Section 357 fixes the commencement date for Tribunal winding up. The winding up is deemed to commence at the time of the presentation of the petition for the winding up. This date is critical for the operation of avoidance provisions, the freezing of dispositions (s. 334), the calculation of preferential periods, and related machinery.

sections.heading: Deemed commencement
sections.body: Winding up by the Tribunal is deemed to commence at the presentation of the petition.

provisions.title: Commencement of winding up by Tribunal

examples.title: Relation-back
examples.body: A petition is presented on 1 March and the order is made on 1 June. Under s. 357 the winding up is deemed to have commenced on 1 March for the purposes of void dispositions and related rules.

hypotheticals.question: Does commencement wait until the winding-up order?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 357 deems commencement at the presentation of the petition.

misconceptions.trap: Commencement is the date of the winding-up order.
misconceptions.correction: For Tribunal winding up, commencement is deemed to be the presentation of the petition.
